correctness.rationale: The centered unit-incidence zonotope in H has d=N-1. For each oriented bond S|T, the induced Euclidean facet area is sqrt(st) tau(G[S])tau(G[T]), its support distance k sqrt(N/st)/2, and total volume sqrt(N)tau(G); these independently yield cone mass k tau(G[S])tau(G[T])/(2d tau(G)). Cactus minimal cuts are exactly one bridge or two edges of the same cycle. Their spanning-tree ratios are respectively 1 and 1/ell, giving claimed masses, full facet counts, sum-one, and equal-mass iff. Independently enumerated a two-triangle bridge cactus: tau=9, 2 masses 1/10 and 12 masses 1/15, totaling one. Finite check corroborates; algebra and cut classification supply the universal proof.
